originalTitle: The Polygamist's author says women see themselves reflected in her Netflix hit
title: Zimbabwe's Storyteller: From Dream to Screen!
content:
Hello, amazing friends! Your friendly news reporter from Africa is here with a super exciting story today! Get ready to meet a truly special person from Zimbabwe who wrote a book that became famous all over the world! Her name is Sue Nyathi, and her story is all about big dreams, hard work, and the magic of storytelling.

Meet Sue Nyathi, Our Story Hero!

Imagine someone who loves to tell stories so much that they write them down in big, exciting books. That's exactly what Sue Nyathi does! She is a wonderful writer, also known as a novelist, from a beautiful country in Africa called Zimbabwe. Zimbabwe is known for its amazing wildlife, like elephants and lions, and its friendly people. Sue Nyathi has a very special gift: she can create worlds and characters with her words that make people feel happy, sad, or think about life in new ways. She is like a magician, but with a pen and paper instead of a wand! Did you know? Zimbabwe is in southern Africa and has Victoria Falls, one of the world's biggest and most beautiful waterfalls! It's truly a sight to behold!

A Big Dream and a Brave Step!

Every writer starts somewhere, and for Sue, her very first book was a huge adventure. It's called her 'debut novel' – which just means her first-ever published book. But guess what? It wasn't easy to get her first book out into the world. Books need to be printed and shared, and that costs money. Sue Nyathi believed in her story so much that she decided to pay for her first book herself! This is called 'self-funding.' It means she used her own money to make sure her amazing story could be read by everyone. Isn't that incredibly brave and determined? She didn't wait for someone else; she made her dream happen with her own hands and heart. It takes a lot of courage to do something like that, to invest in your own dream. It shows how much she loves writing and sharing her stories with the world. Her passion for books was so strong that she found a way, even when it was difficult.

The Story That Flew High: 'The Polygamist'

So, what was this super special book called? It's titled 'The Polygamist.' Now, don't worry about the big word! For kids like us, it just means it's a very interesting story about different families and how they live in Africa. It talks about their joys, their challenges, and how they grow together. Stories like this help us understand different ways of life and how people feel. Sue wrote about characters that felt real to people, living lives that many could relate to. She painted pictures with her words, showing readers what life is like in her part of the world, full of hopes and dreams, just like ours. Did you know? Storytelling is a very old and important tradition in Africa! Grandparents often tell stories to their grandchildren around a fire, passing down history and wisdom through generations. It's a beautiful way to learn!

From Book Pages to Your TV Screen!

And here's where the story gets even more exciting! Sue Nyathi's book, 'The Polygamist,' became so, so popular that it turned into a TV show! And not just any TV show, but a 'Netflix hit'! Have you ever heard of Netflix? It's a special place on your TV, tablet, or computer where you can watch lots and lots of movies and shows. Imagine writing a story in your room, and then one day, millions of people all over the world are watching it as a TV show! That's what happened to Sue's book. Her characters and their adventures came to life on screens everywhere. People in different countries, speaking different languages, could all watch and enjoy her African story. This is a huge achievement! It means her story was so powerful and interesting that people wanted to see it move and hear the characters speak. It's like magic – words jumping off the page and onto your screen! Did you know? Netflix is available in over 190 countries around the world! That means Sue's story could be watched by almost everyone, everywhere!

Why Everyone Loves Her Story

So, why did 'The Polygamist' become such a big hit? Sue Nyathi says that when women watch the show, they 'see themselves reflected' in it. What does that mean? It means they feel like the characters and their stories are real, like they understand them deeply, or that the story reminds them of their own lives, their friends, or their families. It's like looking into a mirror and seeing something familiar and true. When a story makes you feel like that, it's very powerful. It helps people feel less alone and helps them understand each other better. Sue's stories help women in Africa and beyond feel seen and heard. They connect with the feelings and experiences of the characters, even if their own lives are a little different. Stories are like bridges; they connect people from different places and backgrounds, showing us that we have many things in common, like love, friendship, and facing challenges.

Writing Books: A Big Adventure!

Sue Nyathi also thinks about how hard it can be for people to write books. She asks, 'who can afford to write at all?' This means that writing a book takes a lot of time and effort. You need to think, imagine, write, rewrite, and do lots of research. And sometimes, you might need money for things like printing, just like Sue did with her first book. It's a big adventure, and not always an easy one, but Sue's story shows us that if you work hard and believe in yourself, amazing things can happen. Her journey from writing her first book all by herself to having it become a famous TV show on Netflix is truly inspiring. It teaches us to never give up on our dreams, no matter how big they seem. So, next time you read a book or watch a story, remember brave writers like Sue Nyathi from Zimbabwe, who bring us wonderful tales from Africa and beyond!
summary: Zimbabwean author Sue Nyathi's debut novel, 'The Polygamist,' which she self-funded, has become a popular Netflix show, making women feel connected to the story and inspiring us with her journey of determination.
whyMatters: This story matters because it shows us that if you work hard and believe in your dreams, like Sue Nyathi did by paying for her own first book, amazing things can happen, and your stories can inspire people all around the world!

originalTitle: Zambia vote counting resumes after pause over alleged attacks on polling staff
title: Good News from Zambia: Counting Every Vote Again!
content:
Hello, my super curious friends from all over Africa! I'm your friendly news reporter, here to share some exciting updates from a wonderful country called Zambia. Today, we're talking about something very important that grown-ups do: voting!

What is Voting?

Voting is a special way for grown-ups to choose their leaders. Imagine you and your friends want to pick a game to play. You all say which game you like best, right? That's a bit like voting! Grown-ups choose people who they think will do a good job helping run their country. These leaders make important decisions for everyone. Did you know? Countries all over Africa have grown-ups who vote to choose their leaders! It’s a way for everyone to have a say.

Meet the Special Helpers

In Zambia, a special group of grown-ups helps with voting. They are like super important referees for a game! We call them the 'electoral commission.' Their job is to make sure everything about voting is fair and square. They help people vote, and then they carefully count all the choices. They want to make sure every single voice is heard.

What Are These Special Papers?

When grown-ups vote, they use special papers. These papers are called 'ballot papers.' On these papers, they mark who they want to be their leader. It's like circling your favourite treat on a menu! Once they mark their choice, these papers are put into a special box. Each paper is a secret message about who someone wants as their leader. Did you know? In some places, people don't use paper. They might vote using a special machine or even on a computer!

A Little Stop, A Big Start Again!

Now, here's some news from Zambia. The special helpers were busy counting all these ballot papers. They were working very hard, looking at every single mark. But, for a very short time, they had to stop. Why did they stop? Well, some people caused a little bit of trouble. Some of the special papers went missing for a short while, and this made it difficult for the helpers to keep counting. The special helpers wanted to make sure everything was safe and sound before they continued. It was like a little pause in a very important game.

Good News: Counting is Back On!

But guess what? The good news is that the special helpers did not give up! They worked very hard to fix the problem. They made sure all the important papers were safe. And now, they are counting votes again! This means that all the grown-ups who voted can be happy. Their choices are being carefully looked at and counted. It shows that even when there's a small problem, people in Zambia work together to make things right. It's like finding your lost toy – you're so happy when it's back!

Why Every Vote Matters So Much

Why is counting every single vote so important? Because every grown-up's choice matters. When all the votes are counted, it means the leader who gets the most choices is the one everyone has picked. This helps the country be strong and fair. It means that the people chosen to lead will know what the grown-ups in Zambia want. It's like when you and your friends vote for a game, and the game with the most votes is the one you play. Everyone feels heard and happy.

Fun Facts About Zambia!

Did you know that Zambia is a beautiful country in Southern Africa? It has amazing animals like elephants, lions, and zebras! Did you also know that Zambia is home to a part of one of the world's largest waterfalls? It's called Victoria Falls, and it's super big and beautiful! Imagine all that water falling down! Zambia is also known for its friendly people and its rich culture. There are many different languages spoken there, and lots of wonderful traditions.

A Bright Future for Zambia!

So, my friends, the important thing to remember is that in Zambia, the grown-ups are making sure that every vote counts. They are working hard to choose their leaders fairly. This helps Zambia grow and shine bright for everyone. It shows how strong and determined the people of Zambia are, even when facing challenges. We will keep watching and sharing more good news from Zambia as they continue their journey to a wonderful future! Hooray for fair counting and strong leaders!
summary: In Zambia, vote counting for new leaders stopped for a short time because some special voting papers went missing, but now the special helpers are counting all the votes again to make sure everyone's choice is heard fairly.
whyMatters: This is important because it shows that even if there are small problems, people in Zambia are working hard to make sure grown-ups can choose their leaders fairly, so everyone's voice is heard and the country can have a strong future.
